basis_refs.q: like as a ditch sunders field from field

ledger.summary: Leaving Vale Turris by a good highway past the Tower and over the valley ridge, they see the Great Mountains and a sea of woodland breaking grey against the mountain wall. The road runs downhill and then along the boundary between tillage and fenced pasture on one side and the wildwood, always on their right, on the other. David keeps Ralph from mingling with the Queen's people. Toward evening the Lord gallops past with Otter's men and, beside him on a white palfrey, the yellow-haired woman Ralph took for the Queen. Ralph realises she is not the Queen; David will not discuss it.
ledger.geography_notes: From the Dale of the Tower the highway crosses the valley ridge, then descends; thereafter the road divides tillage and fenced pastures from the rough edge of the woodland "as a ditch sunders field from field". The wildwood is on the right (toward the mountains), with tall trees; the mountain wall shows from the ridges.
open_questions: Which side is east here? (wildwood on the right suggests the road runs roughly north with the mountains east)
